title: Your Brain Is Lying to You!
teaser: Your eyes have a literal hole in them, and your vision skips like a broken film reel dozens of times a second, yet you never notice either one. This piece shows how your brain edits, predicts, and fills in reality instead of simply recording it.
author: Zainab Salami

title: What If Your Memories Aren't Yours?
teaser: Every time you recall a memory, your brain doesn't replay it, it rewrites it, which means the memories you trust most may be the ones most changed by repetition. This piece uses real psychology experiments, including a study that planted a fake childhood memory in people's minds, to show why confidence and accuracy are not the same thing.
author: Zainab Salami
refs: Loftus, E. F., & Palmer, J. C. (1974). Reconstruction of automobile destruction: An example of the interaction between language and memory. | Loftus, E. F. (1995). Remembering dangerously. title: The Birthday Problem: When 23 people Are Enough
teaser: A surprising probability problem showing that in a group of just 23 people, there is a greater than 50% chance that at least two people share the same birthday.

title: What the Planes Didn't Show
teaser: A surprising story about statistician Abraham Wald and how studying the damage on surviving airplanes led to a completely different conclusion about where protection was needed. The anecdote introduces the idea of survivorship bias and shows why missing data can be just as important as the data we can see.
author: Nour Al-Zahraa Karnib
level: Basic understanding of statistics, probability, and simple data interpretation is helpful. No advanced mathematics is required

title: Can You Untangle A Knot?
teaser: A mathematical exploration of knot theory, beginning with the question of when two tangled loops are considered the same. The article introduces knot diagrams, Reidemeister moves, knot invariants, crossing numbers, and the Alexander polynomial to show how mathematics can distinguish objects that may look deceptively similar.
author: Nour Al-Zahraa Karnib
level: Basic understanding of algebra, equations, and simple mathematical reasoning is helpful.
